use_case_summary: Zenith is building an enterprise IDE copilot for regulated finance clients. Primary requirement: streaming, sub-50ms completion latency inside the editor (keystroke-level perceived latency). Must support model pinning and deterministic rollouts so we can certify models to customers. Data cannot leave customer VPC for PII-containing repo snippets; audit logs and long-term retention (7+ years) are required.
notes:
Lead: CTO (Riya Malhotra) is risk-averse — wants explicit model-version signing and a tamper-evident audit trail. Key quotes: "We need to be able to say which model version generated a suggestion and tie that to a signed release".

POC scope: 4-week pilot inside a VPC deployment. Goals: 1) Avg editor completion latency <= 50ms (95th perc), 2) No regression in unit-test pass-rate for suggested code, 3) Audit events for every suggestion (user, file, repo, model_version, timestamp).

Security asks: SSO (SAML), SCIM provisioning, SOC2 Type II evidence, ISO27001 ok-to-see, KMS/HSM support for key material, option for audited on-prem bundle if cloud VPC not allowed. Retention: separate retention policy per artifact (logs 7+ years, prompts ephemeral by default but flag to persist).

Tech notes from SE call: prefers VPC private with egress deny-listing + NAT for allowed registries. Concern about KV cache privacy and multi-tenant memory — wants per-tenant cache encryption. Interested in offline model pinning (ability to pin quantized model artifact inside their network) and deterministic rollbacks. Wants streaming with incremental tokens to the editor (not full-response delays).

Commercial: Procurement is evaluating reserved capacity vs private install. Pricing sensitivity around sustained token throughput — expecting high concurrency with 2k daily active devs. Mentioned competitor trials (Copilot for Business) but said: "Competitors don't give us the audit fidelity we need".

Next immediate actions: send updated pilot SOW with data residency clause (Leila), deliver SOC2 Type II artifacts (security team), run 95th percentile latency microbenchmarks on customer's sample repo (SE).
